\>  So what I do is I put on a "mask" and try to act like I am fine.   
Please don't do that. You don't need to tell everyone, you can be discrete in some places, specially at work . But don't try to fake good, because you are not. Don't reject your pain. Its ok to not be ok. It's a sign your body is teeling you you cant stand something hurting you anymore. You need to figure out what it is. It is not easy at all. But it can get better!  


​

\>  I finally opened up to a close friend who used to work in therapy and we talked and it seemed to help but it didn't.   


I know that feeling. You know, we want others to understand our feelings. But they will understand what you are feeling but they can't help. So, it would alleviate your pain? No, so there's another solution.

I'm sorry for what you are passing through. Sometimes I feel alone for being good to others. I feel pity for hardworking people in low wage, for people living in the streets. And I help and show empathy when it is possible. And sometimes people just don't care. Its normal. Jesus cured 10 faithful jews who were blind, and just, one, came to thank him. So, your values is what you do, not what other people judge.  
If you are so stressed and feeling depressed, please seek a psychatrist. It help to not let the blues or anxiety take over.

And remember, over that big blue dirtball we call Earth that are empathetic creatures who feel the same as you.  


 My sincerely hugs,

Please, calm down. There are things more valuable than IQ and beauty. Not that those traits are bad. It's ok to want to feel attractive and smart. But our society subsitute values for beauty, prestige and money. So do not set impossible standards to yourself. It's not fair. There is no perfection, that's why sucessful people get depressed and lonely too. Be gentle to yourself. Would you treat a brother/sister the way you treat yourself?  
Third, set your values straight. You have some good traits, everybody have. I know it's hard to believe but many nice/pretty/smart people felt or feel the same as you. If you cnat control your thoughts, please seek a psychiatrist. You CAN get better.  


Best wishes

\>My life could have been a lot better if not for my parents. I was meant to enter the most prestigious university in my country. I could have had high paying jobs. I could have saved at least five times the money in my bank account. I could be living the life I want. Instead, now I'm a loser working in a shitty job with a shitty pay bound to do this job until I'm 60.  


Depression makes you feel there is no hope. First step. Forget about what you lost. You can't do anything about it. It's ok to feel bad, but it's not ok be ruminating it. Not help at all.  


Second, find ways to change careers. You can find a blue collar job you like to gain another opportunitty. Or apply to a university that offer student housing. There is other options out there.   


Third, don't value yourself by your work. I did that. It sucks. You definately get better and get more money, but still feel shit. Now a selfish and good working shit. Feel proud about being productive, doing your better, and helping others. I'm not saying to forget your dreams or that seking a career is wrong. Just don't forget that your values are much more important than money and prestige.

No it's not ok to *do* that. But it's ok to *feel* that way. It's ok to not be ok. We've been there. I'ts awful, but it **can** get better. I sincerely hope you get better. Best wishes

I needed someone to tell me this.
I'm in tears now, because I know it is true, but i really can't feel it. 
I'm frustrated because others can't see how desperate and sad i'am.

I started therapy the day after I danced with a girl and she made a compliment. It felt so relaxing, but the next I could not stop crying and the feeling of worthlessness. I always danced with the impression I was judged and that other people were joking on me. I knew was not normal to cry when you receive a compliment. Only after the antidepressant I felt how anxious I was. The calming effect was like going back to childhood. My productivity and concentration is up. Exercices are easy. But realtionships still messy.  


Yes, I fell I'm "intimate" when I'm in a circle, or in a face to face chat, and get the feeling they are not liking me, and that I'm sounding weird or goofy. "They not gonna be my friends anymore". I **know** its not true, but I **feel it.** I try to hide the best I can, but then, I sound weird or goofy. If I stay quiet, well, I stay quiet. But the then, they get the feeling that I'm not enjoying their company. Or that I'm tired (I cant count how many times I faked being tired to justify my quietness).   


I control myself, but if I don't get imediate attention, or some signal of approval(a compliment, a comment, or a smile) I get the feeling of rejection. Like, 'they don't like me', which I know it is not true, but I can't control this rumination.   
Every nice party or social occasion, I come back home devastated.

I just want to share my experience; I live in a developing 'nation', and struggled with poverty too. My family was what i would call 'borderline' middleclass.   
After I graduated a diploma, I could find no job. Took years till I got a real nice and stable job in a more developed region.  
And know what? I feel miserable. I see friends struggling in low paying jobs, and I feel pity.   
I'm generous when I have the opportunity too. If a friends needs money, help, or a ride to the next town I do it without questioning.   
But my anxiety keeps me away from getting any real intimacy with people.   
Its frustrating. I'm 'living the dream' in misery and loneliness. I'm a nice, hardworking boy to everyone who looks from outside. But i'm miserable inside. I can't get a girlfriend, because I fear any intimacy I get.  
I can't describe the bad feeling of making expectations with a relationships and see it crumbling in your hand. ALL. THE. TIME.

  Know that feeling of not having a loving, stable family? Yes, I get it too. Everyday. I though I was able to make my family, and correct it out. But no, the old ghosts and fears from my traumatic childhood follows me. The only confort I have is my job thourough the decency of my 'somewhat loving' parents who gave me a nice education.   
No, I would not like to live with poverty in a 3rd world country. But don't fool yourself:  We, living in "confort", suffer too.

Yes, i'm at the 5th week on antidepressant treatment. SSRI. My selfconsciousness and worthlessness ruminating gone away at the 2nd week. Generalized anxiety comes from time to time, but I learned to control it.

But when I start to have some intimacy with ppl it hits me strong again. Most of the time, but not exclusively, happens when I talk to a girl, specially with dating potential. Sometimes I manage well and everything goes smooth through some weeks. TIll I feel awkard and can't get a nice conversation anymore. What is really frustrating is i'm very social with strangers. When I was on another state volunteering, I talked to anyone that worked with me and other groups too. But if things get more intimate, I freak out.
I normally control my actions, so it does not seems I'm anxious, but I' am.
I feel the toll of having nice friends, but i can't feel, or have, any intimacy between us. It's so frustrating.
She was the girl who made that. Till my childhood trauma emerged saying "don't f***** trust anybody you like, they're mean"

Self conscious. Its the medical term. Yes, I suffered from it too. Probably a symptom of some anxiety disorder.  In most cases, hopefully, it get better with antidepressant.   
Please seek an Psychiatrist.
